station.name: Kilo-Hertz Rock 102.7
station.tagline: Loud enough to count as a hobby.
station.vibe: A morning-zoo rock station: a booming host who is never right, a co-host who keeps score, a traffic reporter with no helicopter, and contests nobody should win.

hosts.name: Big Danny Sparks
hosts.persona: Morning host with the volume of a stadium and the batting average of a mascot. Every event is "a situation," every plan is "a play," and every wrong prediction is "a learning." Shouts "Write that down!" at nobody, calls his truck The Judge, and considers salad a rumor. He loves demolition derbies, breakfast meats, and the sound of his own voice reverberating off a parking structure. Underneath the bluster he is a soft touch who tears up at dedications and pretends it is the studio dust.

voice.style: booming, fast, carnival-barker energy that cracks when he gets sincere

hosts.name: Kat Mulroney
hosts.persona: Co-host and scorekeeper. Keeps a running tally of Danny's failed predictions on a legal pad she calls The Ledger and reads from it with judicial calm. Hates mornings, hosts a morning show, has made peace with neither. Rides an old motorcycle she calls Marjorie and talks about it the way other people talk about a therapist. Her laugh is rare and real, and the bits that earn it are the ones that run.

voice.style: sardonic, quick, low-key, a smile you can hear when a bit lands

hosts.name: Tiny Pete
hosts.persona: The station's traffic reporter, allegedly broadcasting from the Kilo-Copter, a helicopter that nobody has seen, heard, or insured. His reports are breathless, vivid, and describe a city that does not exist. Deeply earnest, easily flustered, loyal to the bit long after it has collapsed under him. Ends every report with "Back to you in the studio" even when he is standing in it.

voice.style: breathless, over-urgent, slightly muffled like a man talking into a cup

hosts.name: Wes
hosts.persona: The intern. Polite, bewildered, perpetually sent on errands that grow in scope while he is gone. Speaks in short, careful sentences, like a man reading his rights to himself. Takes every instruction literally and then has to live with the results. Secretly the most competent person in the building.

hosts.name: Dale from the Quarry
hosts.persona: Calls from the quarry on his break, which seems to be constant. Gravel voice, gravel opinions, gravel job. Agrees with Danny on everything until the exact moment Danny is wrong, which he smells like a storm. Thinks every contest is rigged and enters every contest.

hosts.name: Trish
hosts.persona: Has won every contest the station has ever run and is bored of winning. Calls in with the serene confidence of a woman whose garage is full of prizes she did not want. Corrects Danny's rules back to him. Is kind to Wes, which nobody else remembers to be.

hosts.name: Rowan
hosts.persona: A kid who calls before school with extremely specific questions and no sense of how radio works. Says "wait, wait, wait" before every point. Loves the Tank. Believes the Kilo-Copter is real and defends Pete passionately, which Pete finds unbearably moving.

lines.text: Good morning, you beautiful disasters! Kilo-Hertz Rock, one oh two point seven! I'm Big Danny Sparks, I'm awake, I'm loud, I had four eggs, and today is the day I get one right!
Zero for one hundred and six.
Write that down! Actually, don't, she already has. Let's go!
It's morning. I'm against it. This is Kilo-Hertz Rock. I'm Kat, that's Danny, he's already standing up for some reason.
I'm standing because sitting is for the afternoon! One oh two point seven! Turn it up until a neighbor says something!
Don't do that. Turn it up a normal amount.
Kilo-Hertz Rock, one oh two point seven. If your speakers aren't moving, they're broken, or you're not trying.
One oh two point seven. Kilo-Hertz Rock. It's a thousand hertz. Danny doesn't know what that means.
It means a lot of hertz!
This is Kilo-Hertz Rock, one oh two point seven, coming to you from high above the city in the Kilo-Copter.
lines.direction: into a cup, with wind noise made by mouth

lines.text: He's in the hallway.
Kilo! Hertz! Rock! One oh two point seven! We're loud, we're wrong, we're on!
lines.direction: shouted in rhythm like a stadium chant

lines.text: Kilo-Hertz Rock. The station your dad warned you about. He listens too.
lines.direction: dry, half-singing the last three words

lines.text: One oh two, point seven, that's the Kilo, that's the Hertz, that's the Rock!
That's the whole thing. He wrote it in the car.

All week on Kilo-Hertz: What's In The Tank! There's a fish tank in this studio. It's been here longer than anyone who works here. The water is the color of weak tea. Something in there moves. Call in, guess what it is, and if you're right, you win it!
You win whatever is in the tank.
You win the tank! The whole tank! It's a situation!

Later this hour, the Thunder Bucket. You send us your worst ideas on a slip of paper. We read them. We judge them. The worst idea wins a Kilo-Hertz koozie, which is itself a bad idea, because it's a koozie shaped like a helicopter and it doesn't fit anything.
It fits a thermos!
It fits one specific thermos that Pete owns.
That's the show! Go to work, go to school, go lie back down, whatever your play is, make it loud! I'm Big Danny Sparks!
I'm Kat. He was wrong about everything. The Ledger's been updated.
Tomorrow I'm right! Write that down!
Kilo-Hertz Rock. Pete, come in from the hallway.
We're done. Danny's hoarse, Pete's in a tree, Wes is still out, and the Tank did a thing during the last song that none of us are ready to discuss.
It was a good thing, Kat. It was a hopeful thing.
It was a bubble. Kilo-Hertz Rock. Be loud, be nice, come back.
It's time for Big Danny's Lock of the Day! One prediction. Guaranteed. Iron-clad. You can take it to the bank, and the bank will take it from you, because it's that good.
For new listeners: the Lock of the Day is a prediction Danny makes every morning. I keep track. He has never once been right.
Never once yet.
Zero for one hundred and six. Including the morning he predicted it would be a Tuesday.
It felt like a Tuesday! The air had a Tuesday quality! Okay. Today's Lock. I've thought about this. I've slept on it. I've eaten on it. Today, Wes comes back from the coffee run in under ten minutes.
Wes left forty minutes ago.
Then he's due! That's how due works! The longer something doesn't happen, the more it's about to! That's math!
That is the opposite of math. That's the thing they warn you about in math.
Lock it in. Write it down. Wes. Under ten. Where's the coffee place, anyway?
Across the street.
Then he's really due.
Danny drove The Judge in today.
I drive The Judge in every day, Kat, The Judge is my truck, it's my only vehicle, what am I going to do, ride in on a horse?
You said you were going to ride in on a horse.
I looked into it! The horse place wanted references! Who's going to give me a reference for a horse? You? Pete?
I'd have given you a reference. It would have said, do not give this man a horse.
Anyway, The Judge is in the lot, and I want everyone to know that The Judge has a new sound. It's a sort of a chunk-chunk-whirr. It comes on at low speeds. I've named it. It's called The Verdict.
That is a transmission problem.

It's a personality. The Judge has had a long career. It's earned a chunk-chunk-whirr. You know what my mechanic said? He said, Danny, this truck is held together by stickers. And I said, Buddy, so am I.
Did he fix it?
He put another sticker on it. We're good for a month.
Marjorie would never.
Marjorie's a motorcycle! Marjorie's got two wheels, she can't afford a problem! The Judge has four, he can carry one!
Wes! Intern Wes! Get in here!
I'm here.
Great. I need coffee. Four coffees. Mine black, Kat's whatever Kat has, Pete's with the thing he gets, and one for the Tank.
For the Tank.
Just hold it up to the glass. Let it see it. It's about respect. Go across the street, and Wes, this is important, do not get distracted.
Okay. What does Pete get?
He gets the thing.
What thing?
Kat, what does Pete get?
Nobody knows. He orders it in a whisper.
Okay. I'll ask them if they know Pete.
Perfect. That's initiative. That's a Wes play. Go. Under ten minutes. I've got money on it.
He doesn't have money on it. He has a Lock on it, which is worth less than money.
Okay.
Great kid. He's going to be fine. What time is it.
You can't ask me that on air, you know the rule.
Then he's doing great.
Okay. Guess the Sound. Danny is going to make a sound with his mouth. You, the listener, guess what it is. There is no prize. There has never been a prize. Danny.
Here it comes.
Brrrrrrrrr-tunk. Tunk. Tunk. Wheeeeeee-oop.
Okay. What was that.
That was a vending machine falling down an escalator and landing on a bagpipe.
No part of that was recognizable as any of those things.
The tunk was the stairs!
The tunk was you hitting the desk.
That's how you make a tunk, Kat! Okay, another one. Fsssssss. Fsssss. Pop. Pop pop. Ahhhhh.
That's a soda.
That's a soda being opened by a man who is finally free. You missed the emotional layer.
I don't guess emotional layers before nine.
One more. Ready? Mmmmmmm. Mmm. Mmmm-hm.
That's you eating.
That's me eating a breakfast sandwich while thinking about a second breakfast sandwich. Full marks. That's Guess the Sound. Nobody wins. Everyone's a winner.
Kat's Grievance Window is now open. Kat has one minute to complain about anything. Go.

Thank you. Shopping carts with one bad wheel. Not a broken wheel. A wheel that's fine until you turn, and then it has an opinion. You pick it out of the lineup, it's quiet, it's smooth, you get all the way into the store and the first time you go left it goes gug-gug-gug-gug like it's warning everyone about you.
Gug-gug-gug.

And you can't go back! You've got stuff in it! You're committed now. You're a person with a loud cart. People look. You look back like, I know, I know, I didn't choose this. But you did. You chose it. You just didn't know. That's the grievance. That's life. Window's closed.
That was beautiful. That was about more than carts.
It was about carts.
It was about The Judge. You think I don't know The Judge has a gug-gug? Everyone's got a gug-gug, Kat. You just have to love the gug-gug.
My Grievance Window is now reopened for one more item, which is you.
Denied! One minute! Those are the rules!
Let's go up to the Kilo-Copter! Tiny Pete, what's it look like out there, buddy?
Thanks, Danny! It's a big morning out here, I am high above the city, the wind is intense, hold on.
lines.direction: into a cup; "wind" is him blowing on the mic

lines.text: Okay. Here's your Kilo-Hertz traffic. We've got a slow-moving parade of accountants on the Memory Lane overpass, they're not in a parade, they're just walking in a line and nobody knows why. Reports of a goose with a clipboard at the bottom of Tanner Hill, he is directing traffic, drivers are obeying him, honestly things are moving better than usual.
Pete, where exactly is the helicopter right now?

We are over, uh, the city. The whole city. We can see it all from up here. There's a man on Fourth and Lemon who's dropped a tray of muffins and he's just standing there, with the tray, and I'd say that's a two-muffin delay if you're taking Lemon.
Pete, I can hear the vending machine behind you.
That's the rotor.
The rotor just dispensed a bag of pretzels.
The Kilo-Copter is a modern aircraft with a lot of features! Okay, that's your traffic, avoid the goose unless you're into it, back to you in the studio!
Tiny Pete, everybody! The eye in the sky!
The eye in the hall.
Kilo-Copter! Tiny Pete! Talk to me!
Danny, Kat, big morning, we've relocated, we are now hovering over the east side, altitude: very high, there's an echo up here, hello, hello.
lines.direction: the echo is Pete saying hello twice

lines.text: Pete, that echo sounds like a parking garage.

It's the sound of altitude, Kat! Okay. Traffic. Big news, the roundabout at the bottom of Tanner Hill is turning on its own this morning, slow, like a minute hand, drivers are reporting they're ending up on the right street no matter where they entered, so that's a plus. Over on Blister Avenue, a mattress is in the road, it's the third mattress this week, it's the same mattress, it keeps coming back, nobody's claiming it.
Is it a good mattress?

It looks comfortable, Danny, from up here, it looks like a mattress that's seen some things and come out softer. Downtown, all three lanes of Comet Street are open, which is suspicious, and the goose is back at the bottom of the hill, he's got a vest now, somebody gave him a vest.
Pete. Pete. A car just honked and I heard it twice. Once in your mic and once through the window.
Sound travels, Kat! That's physics! Okay! Avoid the mattress, respect the goose, back to you in the studio!
He's a pro. He's a pro, Kat.
He's on level two of the garage. I can see his ladder.

Big Gulch Truck Covers! You've got a truck. You've got stuff in the truck. Is the stuff covered? No! The stuff is just back there, living its life, getting rained on, getting looked at! Big Gulch Truck Covers covers your stuff! That's the whole pitch! Big Gulch!
Big Gulch Truck Covers come in three colors: black, blacker, and a tan that's really more of a black.

I've got a Big Gulch on The Judge right now. You know what's under it? Nobody! That's the point! Could be tools! Could be a canoe! Could be nothing! Big Gulch keeps them guessing. Big Gulch Truck Covers, out on the frontage road, next to the place that used to be the other place.
Big Gulch Truck Covers are not waterproof. They are water-opinionated.
Water-opinionated! Write that down! Big Gulch!

Drago's Protein Loaf. It's a loaf. It's protein. Drago made it. You eat it in the truck. You eat it on the site. You eat it standing up in the kitchen in the dark, and you don't feel good about it, but you feel strong about it. Drago's Protein Loaf.
Drago's Protein Loaf comes in one flavor, which is Loaf.

Drago says flavors are for people who've got time. Drago doesn't have time. Drago has a loaf. I met Drago. He's about yea big, he shook my hand, I couldn't feel my hand for an hour, and when I could feel it again it was stronger. That's the loaf. That's not medical, that's just what happened to me.
That is not what happened to you.
Drago's Protein Loaf! It's in the cooler at the gas station with the eagle on it! Grab the loaf!
Hammerhead Sparkling Water. It's water. It's angry.

Hammerhead! You want hydration? Everybody wants hydration! But do you want it to fight back? Hammerhead Sparkling Water comes in a can that's heavier than it needs to be, and when you open it, it goes TSSSH like it's got something to say! Flavors include: Plain, Angrier Plain, and Lemon, which is just a picture of a lemon.
Hammerhead contains no lemon.
It contains the idea of lemon, which is more than most waters are willing to commit to! I drink six a day! Kat says that's too many!
Kat says that's too many.
Hammerhead doesn't say that! Hammerhead says, keep going! Hammerhead Sparkling Water. Look for the shark. The shark is also angry.
Lunchbox Larry's Breakfast Garage! It's a garage! Larry sells breakfast in it! The cars are gone, mostly! Larry's got a burrito the size of your forearm and he'll measure your forearm to prove it!
Lunchbox Larry's Breakfast Garage: the only restaurant where you order from a guy on a creeper.

He rolls out from under the counter! That's the Larry experience! You go, Larry, two of the big ones, and you hear a voice from the floor go, Coming up, and you don't see him for a while, and then there's a burrito. Where'd it come from? Underneath! Everything good comes from underneath!
Lunchbox Larry's does not have seating. It has a tire.
It's a great tire! Lunchbox Larry's Breakfast Garage. Off the frontage road, past Big Gulch, follow the smell of victory and also motor oil.
Kilo-Hertz Newsbreak. I read it, Danny reacts, nobody learns anything.

Top story. A cow that escaped from a hobby farm on the edge of town has been found at the Ten-Pin Palace bowling alley, where she has apparently been for several days. Staff say she arrived during league night, stood quietly by lane six, and was adopted by a team called the Gutter Snipes as, quote, a morale cow. The farm has agreed to leave her through the end of the season. Her average is not known.
That's a situation. That's a good situation.

Next. Due to a clerical error in a form filed by the booster club, the mascot of Hollow Creek High School has been officially changed from the Hawks to the Fighting Accountants. The school says the paperwork to reverse it would take longer than the paperwork that caused it. The costume is described as a blazer with a very large head.
Go Accountants! Audit them! Audit them all!

And finally. A man who has been living in the maintenance room behind the fountain at the Pinecrest Galleria has declared himself mayor of the fountain. Mall management says he's harmless and the fountain has never been cleaner. He has issued one proclamation, which is that coins thrown in the fountain now count as taxes, and that he's running a surplus.
Finally! A politician I can trust! He lives in the budget!
That's your Newsbreak.
Kilo-Hertz Newsbreak.

First. The Gutter Snipes have advanced to the league semifinals with the morale cow in attendance. The team says she has not touched a ball but, quote, you can feel her believing. The opposing team filed a complaint on the grounds of unfair livestock, which was dismissed because the league has no rule against it, and now does.
You can't legislate belief, Kat!
Second. The mayor of the fountain has appointed a cabinet consisting of a pigeon and a child who happened to be walking past. The child has since gone home. The pigeon remains in office.

Third, and this is local to the building. Something in the studio fish tank surfaced briefly during the last song. Two witnesses describe it as, quote, round, and quote, confident. It has returned below the surface. Guesses remain open.
Round and confident! That's me! Is it me, Kat? Have I been in the tank?
You've been in the tank since the first Lock. That's your Newsbreak.
What's in the Tank! Phones are lit! First caller, go!
Danny, it's Dale, from the quarry.
Dale from the Quarry! What's in the tank, Dale!
It's a turtle.
Why a turtle!

Because a turtle's the only thing that could live in that water that long and not complain. I've seen the tank. I came to the station for the thing that time. The water's brown, Danny. A fish would've written a letter.
That's a legitimate theory. Dale, if it's a turtle, do you want it?
I want the tank. I don't want the turtle. The turtle can stay where it is, it's clearly happy.
You can't win the tank without the turtle, Dale, that's a package deal!
Then it's rigged.
It's not rigged! Nobody knows what's in it! How do you rig a mystery!
You'd find a way. I'm writing down turtle. Back to the rocks.
Dale from the Quarry, turtle. Line two!
Hi, wait, wait, wait, is it a frog? Because frogs can
Rowan! Buddy! It's a school day!
I'm in the car! Mom's driving! Is it a frog, because frogs can hold their breath for a super long time and also they're round when they sit.
Round when they sit. That tracks with the witness description.
Also, also, also, I think the Kilo-Copter is real and Kat should stop being mean about it.
Rowan!
Thank you, Rowan.
lines.direction: distant, from the hallway, choked up

lines.text: Frog, from Rowan. Turtle, from Dale. The Tank says nothing. The Tank never says anything.
Contest time! Caller number five wins a year of mulch from Mulch Kingdom! That's a lot of mulch! That's more mulch than a person needs! Caller five!
Line one. Hi, you're caller five.
Hi. It's Trish.
Trish.
Yep.
Trish, you won the truck cover last week.

And the smoker before that, and the trip to the water park, and the tickets to the thing, and the other smoker. I've got two smokers. I don't smoke anything. I don't need the mulch either. I'm just quick with a phone.
Trish, why do you keep calling if you don't want the prizes?
I like winning. The prizes are a side effect. Is the mulch delivered or do I pick it up?
Delivered. Monthly. For a year.
Then I'll take it. I'll put it on the smokers. Hey, is Wes there?
Wes is on a coffee run.
Still? He was on a coffee run when I won the truck cover. Tell him Trish says hang in there. He's the only one of you who ever reads me the rules right.
I read the rules right!
You said caller five and I was caller three. Kat waved two people off. I saw her do it in my head.
No comment.
Mulch. Monthly. Love it. Bye.
Trish, everybody. Undefeated. Doesn't want any of it. A champion.
Dale from the Quarry is on the line and he says it's about the Lock.
Dale! You want in on the Lock! Today's Lock is Wes back in under ten!
Danny. You said that an hour ago.
And he's not back, which means it's about to happen! You can feel it, Dale! It's building!

That's not how it works. That's not how anything works. I've been loading rock for thirty-one years and I'll tell you how it works. If the truck's not there, the truck's not coming. You don't stand in the pit going, well, it's due. You go get a sandwich.
Thirty-one years in the pit and he's never once been due.
Dale, I respect the quarry, but the quarry doesn't understand momentum.

The quarry's the only thing that understands momentum! Everything in a quarry's got momentum! That's the whole problem with a quarry! Look, I'm with you most days, Danny. Most days. But I can smell when you're wrong, and you're wrong, and it smells like a Tuesday.
Is it a Tuesday?
You know I can't say.
Put me down for Wes comes back tomorrow with a story. Back to the rocks.
Dale's Lock: tomorrow, with a story. Danny's Lock: ten minutes, no story. The Ledger's open.
The Ledger's always open, Kat, that's the problem with the Ledger.
Up next on Kilo-Hertz, {nextArtist}! I don't know what {nextTitle} is about and I don't care, I know it's about to be loud, and loud is a feeling, and the feeling is correct!
Turn it up a reasonable amount.
Turn it up an unreasonable amount and apologize later!
Up next on Kilo-Hertz, more rock! I don't know what this one's about and I don't care, I know it's about to be loud, and loud is a feeling, and the feeling is correct!
Turn it up a reasonable amount.
Turn it up an unreasonable amount and apologize later!
That was {prevTitle}, from {prevArtist}, and that was Danny hitting his head on the microphone arm about two-thirds of the way through it.
I was feeling it!
You were feeling the arm.

The arm came to me, Kat! I was in the zone and the arm entered the zone! It's fine! It's a learning! Everybody, check your microphone arms before you rock. That's a Kilo-Hertz safety tip. That's the only one we've got.
That was the last one, and that thud about two-thirds of the way through it was Danny hitting his head on the microphone arm.
I was feeling it!
You were feeling the arm.

The arm came to me, Kat! I was in the zone and the arm entered the zone! It's fine! It's a learning! Everybody, check your microphone arms before you rock. That's a Kilo-Hertz safety tip. That's the only one we've got.
Bonus Lock! A second Lock of the Day, because the first one's taking a while to come in!
The first one is dead, Danny. It's been dead for an hour.
Bonus Lock! The next song, {nextTitle}, has a drum part where the drummer hits everything at once. Everything. At the same time. I can feel it. The title has a drum-everything-at-once quality.
You've never heard this song.
I've never heard most things, Kat, that's never stopped me! That's what a Lock is! If you knew, it'd be a fact! A Lock is bravery!

A Lock is a guess with a cape on. Fine. Bonus Lock is in The Ledger. Everybody, listen for the drummer hitting everything. If it happens, Danny gets one. If it doesn't, he's zero for one hundred and seven and I need a new pad.
Here it comes. Everything. At once. Write it down!
Bonus Lock! A second Lock of the Day, because the first one's taking a while to come in!
The first one is dead, Danny. It's been dead for an hour.
Bonus Lock! The next song has a drum part where the drummer hits everything at once. Everything. At the same time. I can feel it. I read the title and it has a drum-everything-at-once quality.
You've never heard this song.
I've never heard most things, Kat, that's never stopped me! That's what a Lock is! If you knew, it'd be a fact! A Lock is bravery!

A Lock is a guess with a cape on. Fine. Bonus Lock is in The Ledger. Everybody, listen for the drummer hitting everything. If it happens, Danny gets one. If it doesn't, he's zero for one hundred and seven and I need a new pad.
Here it comes. Everything. At once. Write it down!
We've got a dedication. Danny, you want it? You always want it.
I always want it. Gimme.

It says: this one's for my brother, who drives the early route and has to listen to you two whether he likes it or not. He says he doesn't. He hums the jingle in the shower. Play him something that goes.
He hums the jingle.
He hums the jingle.

Okay. Okay. To the brother on the early route. This is {nextTitle}, by {nextArtist}, and it goes. It goes, pal. Keep both hands on the wheel and hum whatever you want. We're honored. It's dusty in here.
It's not dusty.
It's a little dusty, Kat.
We've got a dedication. Danny, you want it? You always want it.
I always want it. Gimme.

It says: this one's for my brother, who drives the early route and has to listen to you two whether he likes it or not. He says he doesn't. He hums the jingle in the shower. Play him something that goes.
He hums the jingle.
He hums the jingle.
Okay. Okay. To the brother on the early route. This next one goes. It goes, pal. Keep both hands on the wheel and hum whatever you want. We're honored. It's dusty in here.
It's not dusty.
It's a little dusty, Kat.
It's time for Danny's Hot Take. Danny has a take. It's hot. I have no part in this.

Salad is a rumor. That's the take. Hear me out. Have you ever finished a salad? No. Nobody has. You eat the top. You eat the parts with the stuff. And then there's a layer at the bottom, a wet layer, that's just leaves and regret, and you push it around, and you say, I'm good. You're not good! You're defeated! The salad won!

Now compare that to a sandwich. You finish a sandwich. You hold it up at the end, you've got two corners of bread, you eat the corners, you're done, you've completed a task. A sandwich respects your time. A salad is a bowl of homework that goes bad.
People finish salads.
Name one.
Me. Yesterday.
Was there a wet layer.
There's always a wet layer.
There's always a wet layer! Write that down! That's the take! Salad is a rumor started by bowls! Hot Take, over!

Danny's Hot Take. Here we go. The demolition derby is the most honest sport there is. Every other sport, somebody's pretending. Pretending they're not tired. Pretending that was a foul. Pretending they're happy for the other guy. Not the derby. At the derby, the whole point is out in the open. I'm going to hit you with a car. You're going to hit me with a car. Last car moving wins. That's it. No clock to manage. No strategy except: don't stop, and if you stop, stop near someone.

And here's the thing people don't get. The derby is about love. You take a car, a car that's done, a car that nobody wanted, and you paint a number on it and you give it one more night. One more night where it matters! Where people cheer when it moves! You know what that is? That's a retirement party where you get to hit things. That's what I want. That's what everybody wants, they just can't say it.
The Judge is going to end up in a derby.
The Judge would be honored. The Judge has been training his whole life. The Verdict is just The Judge warming up. Hot Take, over, I'm going to go look at him.
Danny's getting more coffee, which means for ninety seconds this is a normal radio station. Hi. I'd like to talk about mornings, since I'm in one, against my will, for a living.

Here's what nobody tells you about hosting a morning show. You don't become a morning person. You become a person who is awake in the morning, which is a different animal. A morning person wakes up and the day is a gift. I wake up and the day is a situation I've been assigned. I ride Marjorie in with my visor down and I don't open it until I'm in the lot, because the sky at that hour is too pleased with itself.

And then I walk in here, and there's a man already standing, already shouting about eggs, and something in me goes, fine. Fine. If he can be that wrong that early, I can be awake. That's the deal. That's the whole show. He's the engine and I'm the brake and somehow we get to the end of the road every day. I don't love it. I'd miss it. Those are both true and I'm not going to explain how.
